question.prompt: Consider the operation “minus the reciprocal of,” defined by \(a\diamond b=a-\frac{1}{b}.\) What is \[((1\diamond2)\diamond3)-(1\diamond(2\diamond3))?\]

solutions.explanation:
Evaluate the innermost operations first. The grouping matters because \(a\diamond b\) subtracts the reciprocal of its second input.

For the first grouped expression,
\[
(1\diamond2)\diamond3
=\left(1-\frac12\right)-\frac13
=\frac16.
\]
For the second, first calculate
\[
2\diamond3=2-\frac13=\frac53.
\]
Its reciprocal is \(3/5\), so
\[
1\diamond(2\diamond3)=1-\frac35=\frac25.
\]
The second inputs used are \(2\), \(3\), and \(5/3\), all nonzero, so every operation is defined. The requested difference is
\[
\frac16-\frac25=\frac{5-12}{30}=\boxed{-\frac7{30}},
\]
choice A.
solutions.title: Follow the parentheses in the defined operation
